cards.text: Twenty YEARS, friend. That's how long Solomon, king of Israel, spent building two houses: the house of the LORD and his royal palace. Now he has something for Hiram king of Tyre, the man who supplied him with cedar and cypress logs and gold for his every desire.

cards.question: Solomon gives Hiram king of Tyre twenty ___ in the land of Galilee.
Hiram goes out from Tyre to inspect his twenty new towns, and he's pleased with them.

cards.text: He is NOT pleased: “What are these towns you have given me, my brother?” That's the face of a man who opened the cookie box and found crumbs.

cards.question: Hiram gives Solomon's twenty towns a name, and it's still their name to this day. What does he call them?

cards.text: Oh, and Hiram had sent the king 120 talents of gold. ONE HUNDRED TWENTY TALENTS, friend, and the richest thing I ever shared a drawer with was an expired coupon.

Next comes the account of the forced labor Solomon used to build the LORD's house, his palace, the wall of Jerusalem, and Hazor, Megiddo and Gezer. He also rebuilds more towns, plus store cities for his chariots and horses. And Gezer? Pharaoh king of Egypt had captured it, set it on fire, and given it as a dowry to his daughter, Solomon's wife. Some wedding gifts come in a box. This one was a whole city.

That's a LOT of building. And still living in the land are people who aren't Israelites, the ones the Israelites were unable to devote to destruction: Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Hivites and Jebusites.

cards.question: Who does Solomon conscript to be his forced laborers?

answers.text: The non-Israelites still in the land
Men from every tribe of Israel

cards.question: Solomon also puts some of the Israelites into slavery.
Solomon doesn't consign a single Israelite to slavery. Why not?

answers.text: They serve as his soldiers and officers
They pay Solomon a yearly tax
They are needed to farm the land

cards.question: On Solomon's projects, the Israelites are also the chief ___ over the people who do the work.

cards.text: 550 supervisors in all! And Pharaoh's daughter moves up from the City of David into the palace Solomon built for her.

cards.question: As soon as Pharaoh's daughter moves into her palace, Solomon builds the supporting ___.

cards.text: Solomon isn't only a builder. On the altar he built for the LORD, he offers burnt offerings and peace offerings, burning incense with them before the LORD.

cards.question: Solomon brings burnt offerings and peace offerings before the LORD three times a year.

cards.text: So he completed the temple. And now King Solomon assembles a fleet of ships at Ezion-geber, near Eloth in Edom, on the shore of the Red Sea.

cards.question: Hiram king of Tyre sends his servants, sailors who know the sea, to serve in Solomon's fleet.
Hiram's sailors and Solomon's servants set sail together. Where do they go to bring back gold?

cards.text: They bring back gold from Ophir, 420 talents of it, and deliver it to Solomon. FOUR HUNDRED TWENTY TALENTS, friend, and here I am feeling fancy about one gold base.

findings.problem: The baker has no way to reason toward 'terraces'. Card 7's summary of 9:15 left out the supporting terraces, and card 13 says nothing about them, so 'terraces' vs 'gates' vs 'towers' is pure luck. Cards 5 and 19 are already discovery questions, and this minor building detail doesn't move the passage forward. Either mention the supporting terraces in card 7's list of building projects so card 14 becomes an informed guess, or tell 9:24 on a story card and ask about something else.

rule.text: The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question.
